title: Rapid Assembly of Multi-Gene Constructs using Modular Golden Gate Cloning
protocol: Design forward and reverse primers for cloning part plasmids, incorporating flanking nucleotides TTT at the 5' end.
Include a BsmBI recognition site with an additional nucleotide in the primer design.
Add a 4-nucleotide overhang complementary to that of the entry vector.
Incorporate a BsaI recognition site with an additional nucleotide into the primers.
Design a 4-nt part-specific overhang for specificity, along with the template-specific sequence.
Use online software like GoldenBraid 4.0 and GoldenMutagenesis for primer design.
If BsaI or BsmBI sites are present in any part, mutate these sites using a domestication step before assembly.
For integrative plasmids, domesticate any NotI recognition site.
Divide parts with undesirable recognition sites into two subparts near the undesirable site for easier domestication.
Design the reverse primer of the second subpart to contain only the BsmBI site and a 4-nt gene-specific overhang.
Design the forward primer for the second sub-part with the BsmBI site and a 4-nt gene-specific overhang that overlaps with the reverse primer of the first sub-part.
Design the reverse primer of the second sub-part in the same manner as step 1.1.
Introduce the desired mutation(s) at the gene-specific region of either the reverse primer (for step 1.2.1) or forward primer (step 1.2.2).
Include a BsmBI site, a 4-nt gene-specific overhang, and a linker sequence in the reverse primer for fusing two proteins.
Use a longer reverse primer to mutate an undesirable restriction site towards the end of the sequence if necessary.
Perform site-directed mutagenesis to mutate multiple undesirable sites simultaneously if required.
Design the forward primer of the second gene with a BsmBI recognition site and a 4-nt overhang complementary to the reverse primer of the first gene.
Design the reverse primer of the second gene as in step 1.1.
Amplify the parts by PCR using a high-fidelity DNA polymerase from genomic DNA, cDNA, or plasmid.
Check the PCR product on a 1% agarose gel and perform gel purification.
Purify the PCR product using at least a spin column if gel purification is laborious.
Add 20 fmol of each purified PCR product to the Golden Gate reaction mix.
Add 1 μL of 10X T4 ligase buffer, 0.5 μL of Esp3I enzyme, and 0.5 μL of T4 ligase to the reaction mix.
Bring the total volume to 10 μL with ddH2O.
Run the thermocycler program for 25-35 cycles of 37 °C for 5 min (digestion) followed by 16 °C for 5 min (ligation).
Perform a final digestion at 50 °C for 10 min.
Inactivate enzymes at 80 °C for 10 min.
Transform the entire reaction mix into DH5α strain or equivalent Escherichia coli chemically competent cells by heat shock.
Spread the transformed mixture on a lysogeny Broth (LB) plate with 35 μg/mL chloramphenicol.
Incubate the LB plate at 37 °C overnight.
Keep the plate at 4 °C for about 5 h to allow sfGFP development.
Screen the colonies under an ultraviolet or blue light transilluminator.
Perform colony PCR on a few white colonies.
Digest a few potentially correct colonies with BsaI-HFv2 enzyme.
Purify plasmids from the potentially correct colonies.
Confirm sequences by Sanger sequencing.
Determine the number and order of transcription units in the multi-gene plasmid.
Select appropriate connectors for each transcription unit based on their position.
Use ConLS as the left connector for the first transcription unit.
Use ConRE as the right connector for the last transcription unit.
Use increasing numerical order connectors for intermediate transcription units.

Assemble an intermediate vector containing the left connector, sfGFP dropout, right connector, yeast selection marker, yeast origin of replication, and mRFP1 part plasmid with E. coli origin and ampicillin-resistant gene.
Purify the six assembled plasmids.
Measure the concentration of each purified plasmid using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer or fluorescence-based assay.
Dilute each plasmid with ddH2O so that 1 μL contains 20 fmol of DNA.
Calculate the DNA molar concentration using an online calculator.
Measure DNA concentrations accurately for plasmids.
Pipette 1 μL of each plasmid into the reaction mixture.
Add 1 μL of 10X T4 ligase buffer to the reaction mixture.
Add 0.5 μL of BsaI-HFv2 to the reaction mixture.
Add 0.5 μL of T4 ligase to the reaction mixture.
Make up the volume to 10 μL by adding ddH2O.
Run the thermocycler program for 25-35 cycles: 37 °C for 5 min (digestion) and 16 °C for 5 min (ligation).
Transform the entire reaction mix into DH5α strain or other E. coli competent cells.
Spread the transformed mixture on an LB plate with 50 μg/mL carbenicillin (Cb) or ampicillin.
Incubate the LB plates at 37 °C overnight.
Take the plate out of the incubator after 16-18 h.
Keep the plate at 4°C for about 5 hours to let mRFP1 and sfGFP mature.
Use a UV or blue light transilluminator to identify green colonies.
Streak out green colonies on an LB + Cb plate and incubate at 37°C overnight.
Streak out colonies from the LB + Cb plate again on an LB + Cm plate and incubate at 37°C overnight.
Pick colonies that do not grow on the LB + Cm plate for restriction digestions using suggested enzymes (BsaI-HFv2, Esp3I).
Alternatively, use colony PCR for screening.
Purify four part plasmids once intermediate vector is assembled correctly.
Record concentrations of purified plasmids and dilute each to 20 fmol per μL.
Set up the reaction mix following Step 3.1.2 guidelines.
Set up the cloning reaction mix following Step 2.2 instructions.
Transform entire cloning reaction mix into DH5α or equivalent E. coli competent cells.
Plate transformed cells on LB + Cb and incubate at 37°C overnight.
After 16-18 h, take the plate out from the incubator.
Keep the plate at 4 °C for about 5 h to let the sfGFP mature.
Use a UV or a blue light transilluminator to identify the non-fluorescent white colonies.
Streak out and grow 8-10 white colonies.
Perform a colony PCR on the streaked-out colonies.
Purify plasmids from the colonies that test positive in colony PCR.
Carry out restriction digestion using suggested enzyme Esp3I to confirm assembly.
Assemble the left connector (ConLS'-pYTK008) for replicative intermediate vectors.
Clone the sfGFP dropout (pYTK047).
Assemble the right connector (ConRE'-pYTK072).
Integrate a yeast selection marker.
Insert a yeast origin of replication.
Combine the part plasmid with mRFP1, an E. coli origin of replication, and the kanamycin-resistant gene (pYTK084).
Transform the entire cloning reaction mix into DH5α or equivalent E. coli competent cells.
Plate on LB plus 50 μg/mL kanamycin (Km).
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Screen green colonies for red/green color-based screening.
Grow green colonies on an LB + Km plate.
Screen misassemblies by streaking and growing green colonies.
Determine the genomic locus of interest for integrative multi-gene vectors.
Design approximately 500 base pairs of 5' and 3' homology arms for integrating to that locus.
Clone the 5' and 3' homology arms from yeast genomic DNA into the entry vector-pYTK001.
Assemble the left connector (ConLS'-pYTK008) for integrative multi-gene vectors.
Insert a yeast selection marker.
Integrate the 3' homology arm.
Combine the part plasmid with mRFP1, E. coli origin of replication, and the kanamycin-resistant gene (pYTK090).
Insert the 5' homology arm.
Transform the entire cloning reaction mix into DH5α or equivalent E. coli competent cells for screening assembly.
Plate on LB plus 50 μg/mL kanamycin (Km) for screening assembly.
Purify plasmids of the intermediate vector and cassette plasmids.
Record concentrations using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer or fluorescence-based assay.
Dilute each plasmid in ddH2O so that 1 μL contains 20 fmol DNA.
Add 1 μL of intermediate vector to the mixture.
Add 1 μL of each transcription unit to the mixture.
Add 1 μL of 10x T4 ligase buffer to the mixture.
Add 0.5 μL of Esp3I enzyme to the mixture.
Add 0.5 μL of T4 ligase to the mixture.
Bring the total volume to 10 μL using ddH2O.
Transform the cloning reaction mix into DH5α or equivalent E. coli competent cells.
Plate the transformed cells on LB + Km plates.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Perform green/white screening as specified in step 3.2.5.
Purify plasmids from white colonies.
Perform restriction digestions using NotI-HF enzyme.
Screen with colony PCR before proceeding to restriction digestion if necessary.
Design a guide RNA (gRNA) for the desired locus using online resources such as Benchling, CRISPRdirect, and CHOPCHOP.
Clone the synthesized 20-nt gRNA into the pCAS plasmid by Gibson cloning.
Linearize the pCAS plasmid by PCR using a reversed primer pair binding to the 3' of the HDV ribozyme and the 5' of the tracrRNA.
Alternatively, clone the gRNA into the sgRNA dropout plasmid (pYTK050).
Assemble the dropout plasmid into a cassette plasmid with linkers.
Assemble the Cas9 TU with the Cas9 part plasmid (pYTK036).
Assemble the Cas9 TU and the sgRNA TU into a replicative multi-gene plasmid.
Linearize 5-15 μg of integrative multi-gene plasmid with 1 μL of NotI-HF enzyme overnight.
Transform 1 μg of pCAS-gRNA and the linearized integrative multi-gene plasmid into S. cerevisiae.
Prepare competent cells using a commercially available yeast transformation kit or following the protocol by Geitz and Schiestl, 2007.
Pellet the cells after recovery, discard the supernatant.
Wash the cells with an equal volume of water.
Plate yeast cells on complete synthetic medium (CSM) dropout plate or yeast extract peptone dextrose medium (YPD) plate with antibiotics, depending on the yeast selective marker.
Incubate at 37°C for two days for colonies to form.
If no colony is observed, incubate for an additional one to two days at 30°C.
Screen yeast colonies for integration by colony PCR47.
Streak out the colony with correct integration onto a non-selective YPD plate.
Grow at 30°C overnight.
Streak one colony from the YPD plate onto a fresh YPD plate.
Again, grow at 30°C overnight.
Streak a colony from the second YPD plate to a YPD plus 100 μg/mL nourseothricin.
Successful curing occurs when yeast cells fail to grow on the selective plate.
Transform 100 ng-1 μg pure multi-gene plasmid into S. cerevisiae competent cells.
Plate yeast cells immediately after transformation onto the CSM dropout plate or YPD plus antibiotic plate, depending on the yeast selection marker used.
Incubate at 30°C for 2-3 days for colonies to form.
